newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end down but off lows.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end down but off lows.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended down but off their lows on Wednesday on bargain-hunting in blue chips led by Telkom and Sampoerna, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index closed down 0.13 percent, or 0.89 points, at 712.50 points after hitting an intra-day low of 708.67 points. Losers led gainers by 71 to 54, with 74 counters unchanged. Total turn-over was estimated at 766 billion rupiah.
"I expect the market is likely to continue mixed on Thursday. Sentiment-wise, potential further selling in tobacco stocks is still on," an analyst with a Singapore-based firm said.
But he said tobacco blue chips Sampoerna and Gudang Garam were good buys with strong fundamentals at their current prices.
Sampoerna closed down 225 rupiah at 8,700 rupiah on volume of 2.2 million. Gudang Garam was unchanged at 9,575 rupiah on turnover of 1.1 million shares.

Analysts said negative sentiment on tobacco stocks was due to concern that growth in the industry had been slowing down. They said the U.S. legal settlement with American tobacco firms had had little impact on the local market.
An analyst with a foreign firm said a slowdown in the tobacco industry should have been anticipated after it had recorded strong growth for the last four years.
Sustained buying interest in other first-tier stocks such as Citra Marga and Bank International Indonesia had prevented the index from falling sharply, brokers said.
Bank CIC, which listed on Wednesday, topped the active list with around 19 million shares traded. It was last traded at 1,025 rupiah against its offer price of 900 rupiah.
The debut of Bank CIC had also boosted sentiment towards other small banks such as Bank Pikko, which rose 200 rupiah to 2,325 rupiah in active trade brokers said.
